implementation.declaration: extern "C" Object* PKG_SW1_0057E1D0_THISCALL re_0057e1d0(Object *receiver, std::uint8_t deleting_flag);
implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX, aliased into ESI at 0x0057e1d1 and never read from ECX again; exactly ONE ordinary stack argument, a BYTE, at entry_ESP+0x4, consumed by the callee at 0x0057e210 (RET 0x4). The byte is fixed by three independent reads: 0x0057e1f0's `f6 44 24 08 01` is a TEST BYTE PTR [ESP+0x8],0x1 (the 0xf6 opcode family, a one-byte memory form); the machine ABI record's ordinary_stack_arguments[0] carries sizes [1], read true, size_inferred false; and the record's ghidra parameter list is empty (parameter_count 0) because the byte is consumed by the terminator rather than named. The displacement resolves to entry+4 and not to the saved ESI: ESP is entry-4 at 0x0057e1f0 (PUSH ESI at 0x0057e1d0, ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x0057e1ed), so [ESP+0x8] is entry+4 while [ESP+0x0] is the saved ESI. Ghidra's decompilation names it `byte param_2` with storage Stack[0x4]:1, which agrees.
implementation.receiver_model: an opaque 24-byte run with NO declared member. The machine-derived receiver record enumerates offsets [0, 4, 12, 20] with bounds_only true, and the four displacements the body reaches are exactly those four, so nothing forces a name -- and because the record says where the body was seen reaching and not which member is which, a member name would be a claim it can neither confirm nor refute. Each access in the body is therefore a displacement. 24 bytes is fixed by this body alone: 0x0057e1d6 reads four bytes at +0x14, so the object must be at least 0x18, and the matching constructor at 0x0057a6d0 (read from the image) writes a dword at +0x14, which agrees. Both numbers are written in decimal in the header because the source span's hexadecimal literals are compared against the listing's and the listing contains no 0x18.
implementation.dispatch_model: none, and none declared. The body has no indirect transfer: abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, and the 23 instructions contain no register- or memory-operand transfer. The two constants the body STORES are dispatch-table ADDRESSES (see evidence.vtable_note), but the body never READS a word through one, so no slot boundary is declared anywhere in this model and the receiver's +0x00 is not named as a member. The record's vtable association (vtable:0x013f57f8, this body at that table's own displacement +0x70) is recorded here for the integrator and is deliberately NOT modelled.
implementation.dependency_note: the one direct callee, 0x00f47380, is declared extern in the package header and defined as an observer in the package's own model test. No other package's header is included. 0x00f47380 is not owned by this package and this package asserts nothing about it beyond what its own seven instruction bytes fix: one stack word read at [ESP+0x4], a null check that returns early, a global loaded from 0x016c8b44, a call to 0x009276c0, and a bare `RET` with no immediate. mechanics.body_shape: alias the receiver into ESI; read the two dwords at the receiver's +0x0c and +0x14; subtract them, clear the low bit of the difference, and skip the release unless the SIGNED result exceeds 2; skip it also when the +0x0c word is 0; otherwise hand that word to 0x00f47380. Then test bit 0 of the single stack byte, write 0x013ef094 to the receiver's +0x04 and 0x013eb938 to its +0x00, and -- if the bit was set -- hand the receiver itself to the same callee. Finally put the receiver in EAX and return past one argument word.

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 23 instructions. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk: PUSH ESI at 0x0057e1d0 takes it to -4; PUSH EAX at 0x0057e1e7 and the CALL at 0x0057e1e8 take it to -12 across the call, so the callee's [ESP+0x4] is the pushed word and the callee's bare RET leaves it at -8; ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x0057e1ed returns it to -4. 0x0057e1f0's [ESP + 0x8] is then +4, i.e. entry+4. The PUSH ESI / CALL at 0x0057e204..0x0057e205 and ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x0057e20a repeat the same pattern and return to -4; POP ESI at 0x0057e20f lands on 0; RET 0x4 then consumes the return address and the one argument word and lands at +8. The frame balances exactly.
frame_resolution.corroboration: two independent agreements. (1) The only stack slot the body writes is entry+4 (read at 0x0057e1f0) and the only thing it pushes is ESI, which it pops back at 0x0057e20f, so the two cannot be confused for one another: a reading that put the flag at entry-4 would be reading the saved register. (2) The argument count is confirmed from the other end -- `RET 0x4` drops four bytes, and 0x0057e1f0 is the single instruction that reads an argument slot at all, so there is exactly one.

slots.entry-4: the saved ESI, pushed at 0x0057e1d0 and restored at 0x0057e20f. Nothing ever reads it, so it cannot be a parameter and it is not part of the machine's observable surface.
slots.entry+4: the one ordinary argument, a BYTE, read once at 0x0057e1f0 and never written. The record's abi.ordinary_stack_arguments[0] describes exactly this slot: observed true, ordinal 1, read true, written false, sizes [1], size_inferred false.

receiver_displacement.0x00: WRITTEN at 0x0057e1fc (MOV dword ptr [ESI],0x13eb938). The listing prints it bare, with no displacement, and the model writes it as a decimal 0 for that reason -- see validation.expected_reasons.CONSTANTS. It is never read by this body, which is why no slot boundary is declared for it even though a dispatch-table address is stored there.
receiver_displacement.0x04: WRITTEN at 0x0057e1f5 (MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x4],0x13ef094). Never read by this body.
receiver_displacement.0x0c: READ at 0x0057e1d3 into EAX. Used three more times without any dereference: SUB at 0x0057e1d9, TEST at 0x0057e1e3, PUSH at 0x0057e1e7. It is therefore a VALUE used as a pointer, and the model converts the word to a pointer exactly once, at the read.
receiver_displacement.0x14: READ at 0x0057e1d6 into ECX, then only ever the right-hand side of the SUB at 0x0057e1d9. Four bytes, so the receiver is at least 0x18 bytes.

mechanics.branch_signedness: THE load-bearing fact of this body, and the one place Ghidra's decompilation is wrong. 0x0057e1de/0x0057e1e1 are `CMP ECX,0x2` / `JLE 0x0057e1f0`, and the 0x7E opcode is the SIGNED less-or-equal. ECX at that point is `([ESI+0x14] - [ESI+0x0c]) & 0xfffffffe`, computed with 32-bit wraparound; the AND clears bit 0 and does NOT clear bit 31. A difference with bit 31 set is therefore NEGATIVE as a signed 32-bit value, hence <= 2, hence the release is skipped. Ghidra's decompilation writes the same test in C as `(2 < (param_1[5] - iVar1 & 0xfffffffeU))`, where the `U` suffix makes the comparison UNSIGNED, so it releases on exactly the inputs this body skips. The model reads the value as signed, and the model test drives seven inputs of which four are ones where the two readings disagree (deltas -2, -4, 0x80000000 and 0).
mechanics.control_flow: three conditional branches and no other transfer, all with absolute targets inside the recovered body span 0x0057e1d0..0x0057e212: JLE 0x0057e1f0 at 0x0057e1e1 (rel8 0x0d), JZ 0x0057e1f0 at 0x0057e1e5 (rel8 0x09) and JZ 0x0057e20d at 0x0057e202 (rel8 0x09). The graph closes inside the span. There is no unconditional jump, so unlike the reference package's shape there is no intra-procedural edge to exclude from a call set.
mechanics.arm_decision: two independent gates in a fixed order, and the order is the machine's. (1) 0x0057e1e1 skips the release unless `signed32((end - begin) & 0xfffffffe) > 2`. (2) 0x0057e1e5 skips it also when begin == 0. The second gate is a separate instruction with its own branch and the model keeps it separate: folding the null test into the span test would be right here by accident and wrong the moment the two were reordered. Then, after both stores, (3) 0x0057e202 releases the receiver itself iff bit 0 of the stack byte is set.
mechanics.write_ordering: the flag test at 0x0057e1f0 is read BEFORE both stores, the stores are unconditional and run on BOTH arms, and the branch that consumes the flag is at 0x0057e202 -- after them. So on the release path the receiver has ALREADY been overwritten with both dispatch-table addresses by the time 0x00f47380 is handed the receiver. The model reproduces that order, and the model test's observer samples the two words from inside the call to check it: a model that moved either store past the release is killed, while a model that moved it to a different slot entirely is killed by the post-call value checks.
mechanics.thunk_relationship: 0x0057a700 is `SUB ECX,0x4` (83 E9 04) and 0x0057a703 is `JMP 0x0057e1d0` (E9 C8 3A 00 00), and that pair is the ONLY reference to this VA in the program: get_xrefs_to 0x0057e1d0 returns exactly one, an UNCONDITIONAL_CALL from 0x0057a703, and the target record's own callers list is empty because Ghidra has no function defined at 0x0057a700. The consequence is exact: a caller that holds P enters THIS body with ECX = P-4. The two stores therefore land at P-4 and P, and the run pair is read from P+0x08 and P+0x10. Both 0x0057a700 and 0x0057e1d0 are also adjacent entries of the table at 0x013f57f8 -- 0x013f585c holds 0x0057a700 and 0x013f5868 holds 0x0057e1d0, i.e. that table's own displacements +0x64 and +0x70, and that table is what this target's record names. That table's run of code pointers also contains all six of the analogues the target record lists (0x005737d0, 0x00585890, 0x00585d10, 0x00588570, 0x0058ac10, 0x0058b650), which corroborates that the record's shared_vtable match basis is the right reading of it. What the class graph IS, and which of the two table entries is the adjusting one, is not settled by this body and is not claimed. The model test models the thunk as a plain function taking the caller's pointer, because that is the whole of what its two instructions do, and drives it against four planted decoys.
mechanics.matching_constructor: 0x0057a6d0 (0x0057a6d0..0x0057a6ff, read directly from the image) is a constructor-shaped body for the same object: it stores 0x013f585c to the receiver's +0x00, 0x013f5858 to its +0x04, 0x01667bac to its +0x0c and to its +0x10, and 0x01667bae to its +0x14, then RETs. That corroborates the 24-byte size and confirms that the two words this destructor reads at +0x0c and +0x14 are words the matching constructor writes. It is corroboration only: this package does not depend on it, models nothing from it, and its own receiver would be the four-bytes-higher pointer given the same thunk relationship. It is recorded because a reviewer will want to know the two bodies are a pair and not two coincidences.
mechanics.not_modelled: the saved-ESI push and pop (no observable -- nothing reads the slot); the relative order of the two stores (no instruction observes memory between 0x0057e1f5 and 0x0057e1fc and the model test adds no instrumentation there, so it is reproduced from the listing and NOT asserted); and the identity of 0x00f47380, which the bridge could not decompile at all and which this package therefore uses only through the seven bytes of its own body.
mechanics.globals: none reached by this body. The two absolute operands it names are the IMMEDIATE constants of the two MOV-immediate stores -- 0x013ef094 and 0x013eb938 -- and both are addresses it WRITES into the receiver rather than storage it loads from; they are written literally in the model so that the source-vs-listing constant and data-address comparisons have something to compare. The one global on the release path, 0x016c8b44, is read by 0x00f47380 at 0x00f47388 and not by this body; it is recorded in the package header next to that callee. The record's dependencies.globals and dependencies.external_callees are both empty, and xref_export data_reference_count is 0.

direct_call_1.convention: cdecl (its last byte at 0x00f47394 is C3, a RET with no immediate, so it returns without touching ESP)
direct_call_1.arguments: one word, the dword the body READ at the receiver's +0x0c (0x0057e1d3 into EAX, 0x0057e1e7 PUSH EAX). It is the word's CONTENTS, not the address of the word and not the receiver.
direct_call_1.return: nothing; EAX is dead on this path and is overwritten at 0x0057e1d6, 0x0057e1d9 and 0x0057e1f5 before anything reads it
direct_call_1.guard: reached only when signed32(([ESI+0x14] - [ESI+0x0c]) & 0xfffffffe) > 2 (0x0057e1e1) AND the word is non-zero (0x0057e1e5)

direct_call_2.convention: cdecl, the same callee and the same terminator
direct_call_2.arguments: one word, the receiver itself: 0x0057e1d1 aliased ECX into ESI, 0x0057e204 PUSH ESI, and 0x0057e20d confirms ESI is still the entry pointer by moving it into the return register. It is the pointer this body was ENTERED with -- which, through the 0x0057a700 thunk, is the caller's pointer minus four.
direct_call_2.guard: reached only when bit 0 of the single stack byte is set (0x0057e1f0 / 0x0057e202), and only AFTER both stores at 0x0057e1f5 and 0x0057e1fc have already written the receiver

mechanics.return_semantics_machine: 0x0057e20d is `MOV EAX,ESI`, one unconditional four-byte store of the receiver alias into the return register, and it is reached on BOTH paths: 0x0057e202's branch target IS this instruction, so the no-release path falls through to it and the release path lands on it after 0x00f47380 has returned. Nothing overwrites EAX between the two paths and 0x0057e20f (POP ESI) and 0x0057e210 (RET 0x4) do not touch it. So the return value is the receiver on every path, and the model returns `receiver` rather than void. The record's own phrase for the same observation is abi.return_semantics = 'unclassified_in_EAX' -- a value left in EAX that no record classifies -- and ghidra_function.return_type is 'undefined' with return_type_resolved false. The decompiler, by contrast, prints `return param_1;`, which agrees with this model and is stronger evidence than the record's abstention because it was derived from the listing.
mechanics.receiver_writes: exactly two, and they are the only two: 0x0057e1f5 writes four bytes at the receiver's +0x04 and 0x0057e1fc writes four bytes at the receiver's +0x00. The record's receiver sub-record agrees (written_through 2). Nothing else in the body writes to the receiver, and the model test asserts that by byte-comparing the whole 24-byte object plus an 8-byte sentinel tail before and after every case.

return_semantics.value: the pointer this body was entered with, on every path. Fixed by 0x0057e20d `MOV EAX,ESI` together with 0x0057e202's branch target being that same instruction, which is what makes it unconditional rather than path-dependent. Through the 0x0057a700 thunk the returned pointer is therefore the caller's pointer minus four.
return_semantics.ownership: no ownership is transferred by the return itself. The optional release at 0x0057e205 hands the receiver to 0x00f47380, so on the flag-set path the returned pointer is to storage the callee has just been told to release; on the flag-clear path nothing is released. The model reproduces the call and does not model what 0x00f47380 does with the pointer, because nothing in this repository identifies that callee.
return_semantics.lifetime: the receiver is 24 bytes and lives at the address ECX named on entry. It is not freed by this body unless bit 0 of the stack byte is set. The word at the receiver's +0x0c is released separately and conditionally; the two releases are independent and the second one releases the receiver, not the first release's argument.

evidence.classification: STATIC_ONLY (no runtime observation of any kind; the runtime axis is GATED at 0)
evidence.decompiler_disagreements: ONE, and it is the important one. The decompiler writes the span test as `(2 < (param_1[5] - iVar1 & 0xfffffffeU))`. The `U` suffix makes that comparison UNSIGNED in C, but the machine's 0x7E is JLE, the SIGNED form. The two readings agree on every non-negative difference and disagree on every difference whose bit 31 survives the mask -- that is, on a wrapped negative span, where the decompiler releases and the machine skips. This model follows the machine. See mechanics.branch_signedness; the model test's case C exists for this and for nothing else. Everything else in the decompilation agrees with the listing and with this model: the two receiver words (param_1[3] is the +0x0c word and param_1[5] is the +0x14 word, since Ghidra indexes dwords from zero), the null guard, the order of the two stores, the bit-0 flag test, both arguments, the caller-cleaned calls, the receiver returned, and __thiscall with a byte second parameter. Ghidra also names the two stored constants independently useful: it renders them &PTR_FUN_013ef094 and &PTR_purecall_013eb938, which is its PTR_<target>_<addr> naming rule and therefore its own opinion that the dwords at those two addresses are pointers to functions.
direct_callees: 0x00f47380 (FUN_00f47380), called at 0x0057e1e8 and 0x0057e205, cdecl, one pointer word each
direct_callers: 0x0057a703 -- an UNCONDITIONAL_CALL reference, and the ONLY reference to this VA in the program. It is the second instruction of the two-instruction body at 0x0057a700, whose first is SUB ECX,0x4.

vtable_associations_not_used_as_evidence: vtable:0x013f57f8 -- the record's own association, and the one the target's six analogues were matched on (shared_vtable:vtable:0x013f57f8, score 4). It is NOT used as evidence for anything in this model.
evidence.vtable_note: recorded because a reviewer will ask, and deliberately not modelled. What the machine shows, read directly out of the image: (1) the table at 0x013f57f8 begins at 0x013f57f8 after a NULL dword at 0x013f57f4 and is a run of code pointers; 0x013f585c holds 0x0057a700 and 0x013f5868 holds 0x0057e1d0, so this body is that table's entry at its own displacement +0x70 and the thunk is the entry at +0x64, and the same run contains all six of the record's listed analogues. (2) 0x013eb938, one of the two constants this body stores, is followed by 0x011e06d0, 0x011e06d0 and 0x00517400; the image shows 0x011e06d0 to be `FF 25 68 C4 3C 01` = `JMP DWORD PTR [0x013cc468]`, an import thunk that Ghidra names `purecall`, which is what makes Ghidra's own `PTR_purecall_013eb938` label possible. (3) 0x013ef094, the other stored constant, begins immediately after the NUL of the string " Editor" that ends at 0x013ef093 and its first five dwords are 0x0041d780, 0x0047d670, 0x00461290, 0x00472970 and 0x00472a70 -- a run of .text code addresses. (4) xrefs_to reports 741 references to 0x013ef094 and 609 to 0x013eb938, essentially all DATA references from destructor-shaped sites; a base-class dispatch table shared by a deep hierarchy is exactly that signature. So: both stored constants are addresses of dispatch tables, and the model names them as such. What is NOT settled by any of this and is not claimed: how many slots either table has, which class either belongs to, and the identity of the class this body destroys. The record's own vtable list is explicitly NOT an oracle -- validate withdraws record['vtables'] for exactly this reason, calling it a transitive classifier association that contradicts the xref export outright (356 vtable ids against a vtable_reference_count of 0 on the same record). Nothing in this model rests on it.

IS IT THE SCALAR DELETING DESTRUCTOR, AND OF WHAT. The shape -- two dispatch-table stores, a conditional release of the receiver, the receiver returned -- is the MSVC scalar deleting destructor idiom exactly, and the 0x0057a700 adjusting thunk is what a shared-base destructor entry looks like. But that is an INFERENCE from the shape. This binary has no MSVC RTTI (AGENTS.md records that, and the vtable pass never ran headless), so there is no complete-object-locator column to read, and no record names the class. What the model asserts is only the four instructions' observable effect.

WHAT THE PAIR AT +0x0c AND +0x14 MEASURES. The body takes their difference, clears bit 0, and compares it signed against 2. The mask is a rounding to even, which is the shape of a byte count, but nothing here divides the difference, no element size appears, and no record says what the pair holds. Calling it a count, a byte length, a pointer pair or a vector is all speculation; the model reproduces the arithmetic and stops.

WHY THE COMPARE IS SIGNED. The opcode settles that it is (0x7E), and the decompiler's unsigned C rendering is the discrepancy. Whether the ORIGINAL SOURCE wrote a signed comparison deliberately, or whether the compiler emitted JLE for a source-level `unsigned` test by sign-extending something first, cannot be recovered from three instructions -- and it matters, because on a wrapped negative span the two readings differ. The model follows the opcode, which is the only defensible reading, and flags the gap rather than resolving it.

HOW MANY SLOTS EACH STORED TABLE HAS, AND WHICH CLASS IT IS. Established: both are dispatch-table addresses (evidence.vtable_note). Not established: slot counts, owning classes, and whether 0x013ef094 is a base of 0x013eb938 or of something else. Both tables carry hundreds of destructor-shaped references, which is what a deep hierarchy looks like, and that is as far as the evidence in this repository goes.

THE IDENTITY OF 0x00f47380. The bridge's decompilation of it FAILED ('Decompilation did not complete'), so nothing about it comes from a decompiler. Its own seven bytes fix one stack word, a null-tolerant early return, a global service pointer at 0x016c8b44 and a call to 0x009276c0. That it is a release operator is INFERRED from the shape and from this body using it on both a sub-buffer and the object itself; no record names it. Its callee 0x009276c0 and its global 0x016c8b44 were not investigated and are not claimed.

WHAT WRITES 0x01667BAC AND 0x01667BAE. The matching constructor at 0x0057a6d0 puts them at the receiver's +0x0c, +0x10 and +0x14 -- the very words this body compares and releases -- and they are adjacent bytes in .data (0x01667bac and 0x01667bae are two apart), so the pair looks like two bytes of one four-byte constant stored as two dwords. Nothing this body reads settles what they are, and this package models nothing from the constructor.

CAN A NON-THUNK CALLER REACH THIS BODY. The xref export records exactly one reference and it is the 0x0057a703 jump. A class whose vtable lists 0x0057e1d0 at 0x013f5868 would reach it through an ordinary indirect call with `this` equal to whatever the vtable's owner offset says, and whether that equals the complete-object pointer or the same pointer-minus-four is a property of the class graph this repository cannot supply.
